fact_text: A third-country professional employed by a Kuwaiti private-sector company holds a 'Private Residence (Article 18)' permit, issued first-time by the Ministry of Interior's General Department of Residency. It is legally distinct from Article 17 (government) and Article 19 (business/skilled) residence.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: Kuwait issues a generic 'work visa'. Actually: the legal status is an Article 18 private-sector residence, a specific category separate from Article 17 (govt) and Article 19. Action: confirm the offer is an Article 18 sponsorship, as the rules, transfers and family thresholds differ by article.

entity_title: PAM work permit precedes the visa
fact_text: Before the entry/work visa is granted, the employer must obtain a work permit from the Public Authority of Manpower (General Authority for Manpower). The MOI private work-visa application explicitly requires this work permit as a supporting document.
evidence_quote: Work permit issued by the General Authority for Manpower.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the embassy visa is the first step. Actually: the employer's Public Authority of Manpower work permit is a prerequisite the MOI visa is built on; no work permit means no visa. Action: have the employer secure the Manpower work permit before booking travel or embassy appointments.

fact_text: For a private-sector work visa the sponsoring employer's passport copy must be valid for not less than two years, per the MOI General Department of Residency requirements.
evidence_quote: Copy of the sponsor's passport, provided that it is valid not less than two years

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: only the employee's documents matter. Actually: the MOI requires the sponsor's passport to have at least two years' validity for the private work visa. Action: check the sponsoring entity's documents are in order early, as a defect on the sponsor side stalls the visa.

fact_text: First-time Article 18 residence requires a police/good-conduct certificate that is certified in the country of origin, attested by the Kuwaiti embassy, translated into Arabic, and with validity of not less than 3 months.
evidence_quote: attested from the Kuwaiti embassy and translation of the same in Arabic), provided the validity is not less than 3 months.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a home-country police check is enough. Actually: Kuwait requires embassy attestation plus an Arabic translation, and the certificate must still have at least 3 months' validity. Action: obtain and legalise the police certificate before departure; attestation from abroad after arrival is slow.

fact_text: Passing the government medical examination (health check) is a mandatory precondition to completing the residence permit. The MOI states the health-check result is required before the residency procedure can be finalised.
evidence_quote: Health check result is required to complete the residency procedure

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the medical is a formality done any time. Actually: the residence stamp cannot be completed until the MOI health-check result is in the system, and a failed/incomplete check blocks the Article 18 residence. Action: schedule the mandatory medical (which includes fingerprinting) immediately on arrival.

fact_text: Proof of paid government health insurance ('Receipt of health insurance') is a required document to issue the first-time Article 18 residence, and it is required again at every renewal.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: employer coverage is arranged later. Actually: the paid health-insurance receipt is a hard document requirement for issuing and renewing the residence permit itself. Action: budget for and pay the mandatory health-insurance fee up front; without the receipt the residence will not be stamped.

entity_title: Civil ID mandatory for residency transactions
fact_text: The Civil ID card (issued by PACI) is a mandatory document required to process residency transactions in Kuwait; MOI residency procedures require presenting the original Civil ID card.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the residence stamp in the passport is the main ID. Actually: the PACI Civil ID is the operative identity document required for residency changes, the driving licence, and everyday services (banking, telecom, healthcare). Action: apply for the Civil ID as soon as residence is issued and carry it at all times.

fact_text: A non-Kuwaiti can only obtain a Kuwaiti driving licence after holding a legal residency for 2 years, or as allowed under Ministerial resolution No. 1729/2005 (which exempts certain professions).
evidence_quote: A legal residency for 2 years or according to the Ministerial resolution No.1729/2005

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you can convert your foreign licence and drive right away. Actually: most residents must wait 2 years of legal residency before they are eligible for a Kuwaiti licence, unless their profession qualifies under resolution 1729/2005. Action: check whether the job title is on the exempt list; otherwise plan for a 2-year wait and interim transport.

fact_text: A driving licence issued to a non-Kuwaiti is valid only for as long as the residence permit is valid, and the application requires the original work permit; the licence fee is KD 10.
evidence_quote: All driving license which are issued for the Non Kuwaitis are valid according the residency validity

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a driving licence carries a fixed multi-year term. Actually: for expatriates it expires with the residence permit, so it must be renewed whenever the residence is renewed. Action: renew the licence alongside each residence renewal to avoid driving on an expired licence.

fact_text: Transferring sponsorship requires the cancellation-and-transfer form of the Manpower work permit together with a letter from the Immigration Department approving the transfer; an employee cannot simply move to a new sponsor unilaterally.
evidence_quote: in accordance with a letter issued by the Immigration Department approving the transfer.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you can switch employers freely once in Kuwait. Actually: a sponsorship transfer needs both the labour authority's work-permit cancellation/transfer and an Immigration Department approval letter. Action: do not resign or start a new employer before the formal transfer is approved, or residency can lapse.

fact_text: To sponsor family dependents, a private-sector sponsor must hold a work permit showing a salary of not less than 450 KD per month, per MOI residency requirements.
evidence_quote: work permit for the sponsor in the private sector, provided that the salary is not less than 450 KD.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: any employed resident can bring their family. Actually: family residence requires the sponsor to earn at least 450 KD/month (and specified professions may apply). Action: verify the contracted salary meets the 450 KD threshold before relocating dependents.

fact_text: A residence-permit holder who is absent from Kuwait for more than six months must complete a dedicated MOI procedure (supported by a study or medical certificate) to preserve residency; otherwise the residence is affected.
evidence_quote: Absence abroad for more than six months

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: residency stays valid as long as it is unexpired. Actually: staying outside Kuwait for more than six continuous months can void the residence unless a permit/justification is filed with MOI. Action: if a long assignment or trip abroad is planned, file the 'absence abroad' procedure before the six-month mark.
